messages:
samir: Quick heads-up — while running the monorepo sampleapp locally I noticed it double-sources keys (ORG_API_KEY from my shell + PROJECT_API_KEY from .env). That ends up sending two auth headers and one of our downstreams returns 401 during an open stream, and the SDK currently tears down and restarts the whole stream. Anyone seen similar?

mika: Oof. Not intentional. Can you paste the request headers or logs when the 401 happens?

samir: Paste from my dev log:

```
Request: POST /v1/stream
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer org_live_xxx",
  "X-Project-Api-Key": "proj_live_yyy",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_auth","detail":"project key not allowed for this route"}
Stream: reconnecting -> SDK closes socket and restarts from scratch
```

mika: Ah, we didn't expect both to be present. SDK precedence is currently: env > explicit param > cli flag (whoops). That explains it.

jules: Long term I'd prefer a deterministic precedence rule documented + a CLI warning when multiple key sources are detected. Suggested precedence: CLI flag > explicit SDK param > PROJECT_ENV > ORG_ENV > netrc/legacy files. That keeps local overrides intentional.

alex: For the streaming case, the bigger DX problem is that when a 401 happens mid-stream we close and re-open which loses state. Two possible fixes: 1) non-blocking token refresh hook that swaps headers in-flight and resumes, or 2) a retry-with-offset protocol so the server can resume. I lean to (1) in SDK: on 401 try background refresh and replay remaining requests, do not tear down the consumer-facing socket unless refresh fails.

samir: +1 on the in-flight refresh. Also, can we add a dev-mode lint/warning when both ORG_API_KEY and PROJECT_API_KEY are set? I spent 15m debugging this because sampleapp had a .env checked into repo for the project key.

mika: we can add a small diagnostic at startup: if multiple auth envs detected and not explicitly pinned, emit `WARN devex: multiple auth sources found — using <source>. See docs:` with a link. That should catch most cases.

jules: Also callout: CI builds occasionally fail during key rotation: CI injects ORG key but sampleapp defaulted to PROJECT key so build jobs started failing with 403. If the SDK had a clear precedence + a `--auth-source` flag it would avoid surprises.

alex: Implementation notes for SDK team:
- add AuthSources enum + precedence table
- expose onAuthRefresh hook for async token refresh
- on streaming 401, attempt hook -> replace header -> resume; only escalate if hook throws or returns failure
- emit guidelines in sampleapp README and make the dev Dockerfile NOT include project .env by default

samir: Sounds solid. I'll open a tiny RFC + sample patch for the sampleapp Dockerfile and a CLI warning PR if no one objects.

mika: please cc @dev-tools when you open the PR. Happy to help with the warning text. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-bot: staging build 2026-03-22_18:24 passed (2.4.1)

alex: one more edge case — ephemeral keys (short lived) need refresh token flow. If someone is using ephemeral creds + the SDK auto-refresh, make sure the dev warning doesn't log repeatedly and flood logs. Maybe rate-limit the warning to once per minute per process.

samir: Agree. I'll add rate limit to the warning and include a note about ephemeral flows in the README.

mika: Great, thanks. If you can include a tiny repro (steps + minimal .env) that would speed review.

samir: Will do — thanks all.
